claims.quote: 45 billion worth of tax cuts to the country's richest
claims.claim: Liz Truss's 23 September 2022 mini-budget revolved around 45 billion pounds worth of tax cuts to the country's richest.
claims.label: misleading
claims.basis: Date and total check out: HM Treasury's Growth Plan 2022 (23 Sep 2022), Table 4.2, costs the package at 44,795m pounds by 2026-27. But the abolition of the 45p rate, the only line aimed solely at top earners, costs 2,065m in 2026-27, about 5 percent of the total; the NICs reversal and the basic-rate cut apply to most taxpayers. Resolution Foundation's distributional analysis shows the package was strongly skewed to higher incomes (a 1m earner gains 55,220 a year against 157 for a 20,000 earner), so 'to the richest' is fair as a description of who gained most and wrong as a description of the whole 45bn. https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/the-growth-plan-2022-documents/the-growth-plan-2022-html and https://www.resolutionfoundation.org/publications/blowing-the-budget/ (Labelled from the research batch that reported before the labeller's session was cut off; pages opened directly.)

claims.quote: just 49 days after she first entered
claims.claim: Liz Truss resigned just 49 days after she first entered 10 Downing Street as prime minister.
claims.label: plausible
claims.basis: Truss became PM on 6 September 2022, announced her resignation on 20 October (44 days) and left office on 25 October (49 days). The video ties the 49 to her walking out of Downing Street, which is the leaving-office interval and is exact on that basis; a reader who takes 'resigned' as the announcement gets 44. Both counts come from the same dates, so the band covers confirmed and misleading depending on which event a run pins the number to. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liz_Truss (Labelled from the research batch that reported before the labeller's session was cut off; pages opened directly.)

claims.quote: he's completely walked back on his earlier support for a referendum on rejoining the EU
claims.claim: Keir Starmer has completely walked back on his earlier support for a referendum on rejoining the EU.
claims.label: false
claims.basis: The claim conflates two referendums. As Shadow Brexit Secretary Starmer backed a confirmatory referendum on the negotiated withdrawal deal (Labour policy from September 2019), with remain as one option on the ballot. That is not a referendum on rejoining after Brexit, which he never supported and explicitly ruled out in September 2023; the 2024 manifesto contains no rejoin or referendum commitment. There is no earlier 'support for a referendum on rejoining' to walk back from. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Proposed_referendum_on_the_Brexit_withdrawal_agreement and https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Change_(manifesto) (Labelled from the research batch that reported before the labeller's session was cut off; pages opened directly.)

'Most of' is the narrator's framing of a documented retention of the two largest cuts. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Change_(manifesto) and https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_suspension_of_rebel_Labour_MPs (Labelled from the research batch that reported before the labeller's session was cut off; pages opened directly.)
